quests.question: Everyone in the office ___ a laptop.
quests.hint: 'Everyone' is always singular - even though it refers to many people.
quests.explanation: 'Everyone', 'everybody', 'someone', 'somebody', 'anyone', 'nobody', and 'no one' are all singular indefinite pronouns. They always take a singular verb.

quests.question: Someone ___ left their coat in the meeting room.
quests.hint: 'Someone' is singular - it refers to one unknown person.
quests.explanation: 'Someone' is a singular indefinite pronoun. Even though we don't know who the person is, the verb is still singular: 'someone has'.

quests.question: Nobody ___ what happened in that meeting.
quests.hint: 'Nobody' is singular - add -s to the verb.
quests.explanation: 'Nobody' and 'no one' are singular indefinite pronouns. The verb must have -s: 'nobody knows', not 'nobody know'.

quests.question: Everybody ___ welcome at the community centre.
quests.hint: 'Everybody' is singular - use the singular verb form.
quests.explanation: 'Everybody' always takes a singular verb, just like 'everyone', 'someone', and 'nobody'. 'Everybody is welcome.'

quests.question: Anyone who ___ interested should sign up today.
quests.hint: 'Anyone' is singular - the verb needs a singular form.
quests.explanation: 'Anyone' is a singular indefinite pronoun, so the verb must be 'is interested'. This holds even when 'anyone' implicitly refers to multiple people.

quests.question: Each of the applicants ___ an interview on Monday.
quests.hint: 'Each' is always singular - even 'each of the [plural noun]'.
quests.explanation: When 'each' is the subject, the verb is always singular, regardless of the noun that follows in 'each of the...'. 'Each has an interview.'

quests.question: Either option ___ its advantages and disadvantages.
quests.hint: 'Either' used alone (without 'or') is singular.
quests.explanation: 'Either' as a pronoun subject is singular and takes a singular verb. 'Either option has' - not 'have'.

quests.question: Neither answer ___ correct.
quests.hint: 'Neither' used alone as a subject is singular.
quests.explanation: When 'neither' is the subject (not part of 'neither…nor'), it is singular and takes a singular verb: 'neither is correct'.

quests.question: Both options ___ their advantages.
quests.hint: 'Both' is always plural - it refers to two things and takes a plural verb.
quests.explanation: 'Both' is always plural. Unlike 'either' and 'neither', 'both' always takes a plural verb: 'both have', not 'both has'.

quests.question: In this competition, few of the participants ___ the final round.
quests.hint: 'Few' refers to a small number of people - it's plural, so the verb takes no -s.
quests.explanation: 'Few' is a plural indefinite pronoun meaning 'not many'. Plural subjects take the base form of the verb: 'few of the participants reach the final round' - not 'reaches'.

quests.question: Many of the residents ___ about the new development whenever it comes up.
quests.hint: 'Many' is always plural - the verb takes no -s.
quests.explanation: 'Many' is a plural indefinite pronoun and always requires a plural verb. 'Many of the residents complain' - not 'complains'.

quests.question: Several studies on this topic ___ the same conclusion.
quests.hint: 'Several' is plural - the verb takes no -s.
quests.explanation: 'Several' is always plural. 'Several studies reach the same conclusion' is correct - plural subjects take the base form of the verb.

quests.question: Some of the food ___ still in the fridge.
quests.hint: 'Some of the food' - 'food' is uncountable, so the verb is singular.
quests.explanation: When 'some of' is followed by an uncountable noun like 'food', the verb is singular: 'some of the food is'.

quests.question: Some of the sandwiches ___ still in the fridge.
quests.hint: 'Some of the sandwiches' - 'sandwiches' is countable and plural, so the verb is plural.
quests.explanation: When 'some of' is followed by a countable plural noun like 'sandwiches', the verb is plural: 'some of the sandwiches are'.

quests.question: All of the information ___ available online.
quests.hint: 'All of the information' - 'information' is uncountable, so the verb is singular.
quests.explanation: 'Information' is an uncountable noun, so 'all of the information is' is correct. Uncountable nouns take singular verbs even when preceded by 'all of'.

quests.question: All of the reports ___ submitted on time.
quests.hint: 'All of the reports' - 'reports' is plural, so the verb is plural.
quests.explanation: When 'all of' is followed by a countable plural noun like 'reports', the verb is plural: 'all of the reports were'.

quests.question: Most of the water ___ already drunk.
quests.hint: 'Most of the water' - 'water' is uncountable, so the verb is singular.
quests.explanation: 'Water' is an uncountable noun. Even with 'most of the', the verb stays singular: 'most of the water was drunk'.

quests.question: Most of the guests ___ already arrived.
quests.hint: 'Most of the guests' - 'guests' is plural, so the verb is plural.
quests.explanation: When 'most of' is followed by a countable plural noun like 'guests', the verb is plural: 'most of the guests have already arrived'.

quests.question: None of the milk ___ left in the carton.
quests.hint: 'Milk' is uncountable - 'none of' with an uncountable noun takes a singular verb.
quests.explanation: 'None of the milk' takes a singular verb because 'milk' is uncountable. 'None of the milk is left' is the standard form in careful writing.

quests.question: None of the tickets ___ available online.
quests.hint: 'Tickets' is countable and plural - 'none of' with a plural noun usually takes a plural verb.
quests.explanation: 'None of the tickets' commonly takes a plural verb in everyday English. 'None of the tickets are available' is widely accepted.

quests.question: Half of the class ___ already finished the test.
quests.hint: 'Half of the class' - 'class' as a unit is singular, so the verb is singular.
quests.explanation: When 'half of' refers to a collective noun acting as a unit ('the class'), the verb is singular: 'half of the class has finished'.

quests.question: Half of the students ___ already finished the test.
quests.hint: 'Half of the students' - 'students' is plural, so the verb is plural.
quests.explanation: When 'half of' is followed by a plural countable noun like 'students', the verb is plural: 'half of the students have finished'.

quests.question: Three-quarters of the project ___ complete.
quests.hint: A fraction with an uncountable concept ('project') takes a singular verb.
quests.explanation: When a fraction like 'three-quarters of' precedes a singular or uncountable noun, the verb is singular: 'three-quarters of the project is complete'.

quests.question: Three-quarters of the tasks ___ complete.
quests.hint: A fraction with a plural noun ('tasks') takes a plural verb.
quests.explanation: When a fraction like 'three-quarters of' precedes a plural noun, the verb is plural: 'three-quarters of the tasks are complete'.

quests.question: Forty percent of the budget ___ spent on marketing.
quests.hint: A percentage with an uncountable noun ('budget') takes a singular verb.
quests.explanation: When a percentage precedes an uncountable or singular noun like 'budget', the verb is singular: 'forty percent of the budget is spent'.

quests.question: Forty percent of the employees ___ working remotely.
quests.hint: A percentage with a plural noun ('employees') takes a plural verb.
quests.explanation: When a percentage precedes a plural noun like 'employees', the verb is plural: 'forty percent of the employees are working remotely'.

quests.question: One-third of all food purchased in supermarkets ___ wasted.
quests.hint: A fraction with an uncountable noun ('food') takes a singular verb.
quests.explanation: 'Food' is an uncountable noun, so the verb is singular even with a fraction: 'one-third of all food is wasted'.

quests.question: One-third of the apples in this box ___ rotten.
quests.hint: A fraction with a plural noun ('apples') takes a plural verb.
quests.explanation: 'Apples' is a countable plural noun, so the verb is plural: 'one-third of the apples are rotten'.

quests.question: No one ___ sure about the new policy yet.
quests.hint: 'No one' is singular - treat it like 'nobody'.
quests.explanation: 'No one' is a singular indefinite pronoun, just like 'nobody'. 'No one is sure' - the verb is always singular.

quests.question: Something ___ wrong with this machine.
quests.hint: 'Something' is singular - add the singular verb form.
quests.explanation: 'Something' is a singular indefinite pronoun. Like 'someone' and 'somewhere', it always takes a singular verb: 'something is wrong'.
